title: Histograms group numeric values
summary: A histogram groups numbers into bins and counts how many fall in each bin. A bin is an interval, not a category label.
introduction: A histogram groups numbers into bins and counts how many fall in each bin. A bin is an interval, not a category label. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A histogram groups numbers into bins and counts how many fall in each bin. A bin is an interval, not a category label.

blocks.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.hist([1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3], bins=[0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5])
ax.set_xlabel("Books per learner")
ax.set_ylabel("Learners")
plt.show()
blocks.title: Histograms group numeric values

blocks.text: The three bins have heights 2, 1 and 3. The explicit edges make the grouping clear.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Count the values in each bin by hand.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Changing bin widths changes the appearance of a histogram.
For more detail later, use this [Matplotlib further reading](https://matplotlib.org/stable/users/explain/quick_start.html).
